edit.description: `hookDefaultContract` gains `clause(required("type"), { severity: "required", cite })` beside its `enumOf("type", DOCUMENTED_HOOK_HANDLER_TYPES)` — the docs' Common-fields table marks `type` Required=yes and gives it no default, so an absent one is dead configuration the enum alone cannot see. `Hook.type` loses its `?` with it, the pattern `Skill.description` and `Marketplace.owner` already hold: a documented-required field is mandatory in the interface and clause-gated in the contract. The header's closing paragraph — "An absent `type` passes every guard, the way an absent transport does for an `mcp-server`" — is retired: the analogy inverts here, since `mcp-server`'s absent transport has a documented `stdio` default and `type` has none.

Line 310's `hook({ name: "PreToolUse", command: "temper guard" })` is the one authored hook in the tree carrying no `type`; it takes `type: "command"` or strict `tsc` fails on the mandatory field. Nothing else about that refusal case moves.

`hookDefaultContract guards every documented handler kind…` already owns every claim over the `type` field — extend it with the presence clause beside the enum, so the contract's two clauses over one field are pinned in one place rather than drifting apart.
Regenerated by re-running the memberless emit, never hand-edited — `tests/builtin_lock_frozen.rs` byte-compares the embedded rows against the SDK's own derivation.

The firing case: `BROKEN_HANDLER_SETTINGS` carries a `command` handler with no `command`, an `http` one with no `url` and an undocumented `type`, but no handler missing `type` altogether — add that one and assert it raises `hook.required.type` exactly once, behind the `coverage.checked` vacuity pin the file's other cases already ride, with the enum staying silent on it (an absent field is nothing for an allowlist to refuse). `EVERY_HANDLER_KIND_SETTINGS` stays silent unchanged — every handler there names its kind.
The `hook` row's `required` column goes blank → `error`; the row's `enum` and `when` cells are unchanged.

summary: The hook handler's `type` is documented required with no default, but the contract only enums its value — an absent `type` passes every clause silently.

tests.asserts: a handler carrying no `type` fires one required-severity `hook.required.type` and no enum finding; the well-formed handler of every documented kind still fires nothing
the regenerated `src/builtin_lock.toml` still byte-matches the SDK's memberless emit, so the new clause reaches SDK-less checking
the presence clause over `type` ships beside the enum, both carrying their own cite

acceptance: `cargo test` and `pnpm --dir sdk test` green with the new case red on the pre-fix lock; `temper check .` on this repo's own harness stays clean (every hook in `.claude/settings.json`, both `examples/` harnesses and every Rust fixture already names its handler `type`).
